Status

FinKore Core 2.0.3 stable.

Purpose

This document defines how a Financial Entity progresses through declared domain States.

Requirements

  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-001 — A Financial Entity MUST declare or reference a Workflow.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-002 — A newly created Financial Entity MUST begin in that Workflow's initial State. Import with existing history follows the separate rule in Workflow States.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-003 — Current State MUST change only through a Successful Transition.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-004 — Audit requirements for lifecycle Transitions MUST be declared as specified by Financial Entities.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-005 — A composing domain MUST define the domain consequences of each state.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-006 — A Financial Entity MUST have exactly one current lifecycle State.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-007 — In the bounded Entity representation, an existing observation's missing, null, empty, or non-string current State MUST use FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_INSTANCE. A nonempty string identifying an undeclared State MUST use FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_STATE. Consuming Entity operations MUST preserve Workflow validation priority under WORKFLOW-ERROR-007, including definition validation before instance validation, and MUST preserve existing observations on failure.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-008 — When a bounded Entity Transition Request supplies object-valued guard facts, the Entity transition MUST pass that exact value to the referenced Workflow Transition Guard evaluation. Omission MUST represent no supplied facts. The operation MUST NOT derive guard facts implicitly from Entity data, Approval history, authorization services, wall-clock state, or other ambient state. Supplied facts MUST NOT create a Guard where the referenced Workflow declares none, and failed guard evaluation MUST preserve the complete Entity and supplied facts.
  • ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-009 — In Core 2.0, a supplied Entity Transition facts value MUST be an object. A supplied null, array, string, number, or Boolean MUST fail with FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_CONTEXT according to WORKFLOW-ERROR-008. Omission continues to mean that no facts were supplied. The error and preservation semantics are part of the Core 2.0 contract for the existing canonical finkore.entity.transition operation; no alias or replacement operation is introduced.

Invariants

A Financial Entity must have exactly one current lifecycle State. A Rejected Transition must leave both current State and entity data unchanged.

Guard facts and resulting-State validation

ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-008 composes the existing Workflow guard contract rather than defining a second evaluator. An omitted fact selected by a declared Guard causes the existing FINKORE_WORKFLOW_GUARD_REJECTED result. A valid supplied object is compared under the referenced Workflow's rules and is request context, not Entity data to persist. A supplied object has no effect on an unguarded Transition.

Core 2.0 closes the former malformed-context gap: supplied non-object facts is FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_CONTEXT. It must not be repaired or treated as omission. The priority in WORKFLOW-ERROR-008 preserves every earlier definition, instance, version, State, conflict, terminal, and Transition error, and places invalid context before guard rejection.

After the referenced Workflow has accepted the Transition Request, including its guard evaluation, the complete proposed Entity at the target State remains subject to Entity Validation. A target-State validation failure uses FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED and leaves identity, type, data, State, Workflow binding, and supplied facts unchanged. An earlier primary Workflow failure is preserved under ENTITY-ERROR-004; target-State validation does not replace invalid-State, terminal-State, invalid-Transition, or guard-rejection results.

Examples

Referencing a versioned Workflow under ENTITY-LIFECYCLE-001 also applies WORKFLOW-VERSION-007 through WORKFLOW-VERSION-011. Creation records the initial binding; subsequent transitions and observations preserve it. Existing Entity observations supplied for reconstruction, import, mutation, or evolution cannot lose or derive that binding from a replacement definition. A versioned observation without its required binding uses FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_INSTANCE; a well-formed binding that disagrees with the supplied definition uses FINKORE_WORKFLOW_VERSION_MISMATCH, following Workflow priority and ENTITY-ERROR-004. Failure preserves Entity State, data, and binding.

The specification does not prescribe a production Entity envelope. The conformance convention records the binding inside each versioned Entity observation so the actual output can be reused. Unversioned observations do not acquire an invented version. Ownership of unversioned Entity declarations follows ENTITY-DEFINITION-002, separately from Workflow versioning.

DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED
                  └→ REJECTED

Invalid Examples

  • Assigning APPROVED directly when no permitted transition exists.

Errors

Workflow failures use Workflow Errors; entity-specific constraints use Entity Errors.

Open Questions

  • Historical replay and provenance beyond the explicit observation boundary in Entity Import remain outside the current contract.

Non-Goals

Lifecycle State semantics do not by themselves define Correction, Reversal, Void, Supersession, Cancellation, or Adjustment behavior. Core 2.0 Entity Evolution defines portable correction, reversal, void, and supersession distinctions; composing domains still define concrete lifecycle eligibility and consequences.
